newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zairean police robbed crew - Belgian TV.
newsitem.headline: Zairean police robbed crew - Belgian TV.

text.p: Zairean police detained and interrogated a Belgian television crew for hours in the capital Kinshasa on Monday night and forced them to pay a bribe before releasing them, VTM television said on Tuesday.

The crew -- a reporter, a cameraman and their Zairean driver -- were arrested during an interview with a Belgian aid worker on the situation in eastern Zaire where Zairean troops are involved in a spreading war with ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge fighters.
The three were driven in their own car to the headquarters of the secret police where they were told to strip and surrender their possessions. They were then questioned.
Reporter Chris Michel said by telephone from Kinshasa, "They (the officers) suggested we pay them. We then gave $200. We later noticed they had stolen $300 as well."

He said the crew was released as they threatened to lodge an official protest with the Zairean government. But on their return to their hotel the reporters were blocked from resuming their work, along with other foreign newsmen staying there.
"We are being held hostage in our hotel, although I expect that situation to change soon," Michel said.

Belgian media have said the Zairean authorities are actively keeping reporters from entering the war zone near the border with Burundi, partly in a bid to keep news from the area from reaching not only the outside world but also Zaireans.
